exit_criterion: PROPOSAL.md section 16: "Two models differing only in preprocessing can be compared step by step; an exported model reproduces application predictions within tolerance in a clean environment." Concretely, and demonstrated rather than reasoned: the application exports a fitted PLS model as the three artifacts section 9 names, a script installs nothing but NumPy in a fresh environment, runs the exported snippet against the same spectra, and the predictions agree with the served ones within a tolerance this list states; and the comparison view shows, for two experiments on one dataset, exactly which pipeline nodes differ and what each model scored. The phase ends when both are recorded with their evidence.

features.title: An experiment history, not only the last run
features.user_visible_behavior: The outline lists every experiment this project has run, newest first, with its status, its pipeline hash and its headline metric; opening one shows what it ran and what it scored.
verification: uv run pytest - read_experiments returns every recorded run in order and GET /experiments serves them; the existing /experiments/current is unchanged
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build
pnpm exec playwright test - the seeded project lists more than one experiment after a second run
features.evidence: 2026-09-18. Backend: project.read_experiments(directory, limit) returns every recorded run newest first, in read_experiment's own order so the two cannot disagree about which run is current, and skips a row that no longer validates rather than refusing the history; GET /api/experiments serves a summary row per run - id, status, timestamps, pipeline hash, node count, dataset version, error and the headline metrics - and GET /api/experiments/{id} now opens any run in the history, with `current` still meaning the newest. tests/test_experiment_history.py (3 tests): three runs come back newest first with read_experiment as the head and limit honoured, an empty project has an empty history, and a row whose document is not an Experiment costs only itself - written later than the good one, so a reader that gave up on the first bad row would return nothing. test_the_history_lists_every_run_newest_first_and_each_one_opens in test_server.py runs two different recipes and asserts the order, the differing pipeline hashes, the exact row keys and that every row opens to a record whose snapshot has the node count the row claimed. `uv run pytest` 868 passed 1 skipped; ruff, format, mypy clean. Frontend: useExperiments and useExperimentRecord; the outline lists every run with runLabel numbering from the project's first so a number does not move and runFigure carrying whichever headline the run has, or its status when it did not succeed; ExperimentView renders the record in four sections - what it ran (the snapshot as a node table), against what, what it scored, where - with a failed run's cause in an alert. experiments.test.ts (3 tests) covers the two helpers. `pnpm test` 126 passed; typecheck, lint, build clean. e2e `the outline lists every run, and one opens to what it ran` (runs project, which by then has several runs): the drawn count equals the served history, the newest is first, and opening it shows the record rather than the placeholder. Against HEAD's screens and backend it FAILED at `expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected)` - the outline drew one row however many runs there were. With the fix `pnpm exec playwright test` 58 passed (1.6m). CI found one more thing: the e2e counted the outline's rows with `count()`, which does not wait, so on the Windows runner it counted a frame before the query resolved and saw zero. Polled instead - the claim is the list's state, not a moment - and the runs project passes 7.
features.notes: Pagination deliberately not added: a project's runs are tens, and api.py's note on deferred pagination applies - fixing the shape of an answer before there is a question. The row is a summary because a list of thirty runs each carrying a ten-fold split's index sets is megabytes to draw thirty names; the whole record stays behind experiments/{id}. lineage-comparison is the next thing to hang from this.

features.title: The model artifact: one self-describing file
features.user_visible_behavior: A fitted estimator can be saved as one file that carries the pipeline definition, the fitted parameters, the provenance record and the metrics, and that file can be read back without this application.
verification: docs/model-artifact.md, normative, written before the writer

uv run pytest tests/test_artifact.py - every array round-trips bit for bit; a decomposition carries what it has and not what it does not; a newer schema version is refused by name; five malformed files each give a sentence
The same suite opens an artifact in a subprocess where this package is made unreachable, so the format is proven not to need it
uv run ruff check && uv run ruff format --check && uv run mypy && uv run pytest
features.evidence: 2026-09-18. Format first: docs/model-artifact.md is normative and states the container (a zip of manifest.json and one .npy per array), the version rule, every manifest field, every array name with its shape and task, the prediction arithmetic, and what is deliberately not in it. artifact.py implements it: write_artifact returns the content hash of the bytes that landed and writes through a temporary file; read_artifact refuses a file stamped newer by name, as db.py refuses a newer database. EstimatorResult gained x_mean and y_mean - the estimator's own centring, which _fit_pls1 computed and threw away and folded_coefficients recovered by refitting the chain; that endpoint now reads them, with the refit kept as the fallback for a result stored before #211. tests/test_artifact.py, 11 tests: a PLS below a ten-fold split round-trips its coefficients, x_mean, VIP, loadings, rotations and both index sets bit for bit with float64 and int64 dtypes; the pipeline travels by value and parses back to the same content hash; a PCA carries no coefficients, no x_mean, no indices and a null split, because a reader must not assume an array that absent is absent rather than empty; a file stamped schema_version 4 is refused naming both numbers; five malformed files (not a zip, no manifest, bad JSON, no schema_version, an array the archive does not hold) each give a sentence. The claim that matters - PROPOSAL.md section 8.4's 'readable without this application' - is tested by reading an artifact in a subprocess that installs a meta-path finder raising on any import of chemometrics_workbench, and asserting afterwards that sys.modules holds nothing of ours. Blocking rather than relying on absence, because in a developer's environment the package is installed and a test that merely did not import it would prove nothing. `uv run pytest` 879 passed 1 skipped; ruff, format, mypy clean; frontend typecheck, tests (126) and build unchanged and clean.
features.notes: A zip of JSON and .npy rather than a pickle: a pickle needs this package importable and executes what it is sent, and an artifact is a thing people email to each other. Scores, predictions and per-sample diagnostics are deliberately absent - they are properties of the samples the model saw, recomputable from the model and the data, where the artifact is what you need to use and explain the model. Prediction from an artifact is json-and-snippet-export; recording one in the project is model-registry; no endpoint is added here.

features.title: JSON model and a standalone Python prediction snippet
features.user_visible_behavior: A fitted regression exports as a documented JSON model - the preprocessing steps with their parameters, the coefficients, the intercept and the scaling - and as a self-contained Python function that depends only on NumPy and reproduces the application's predictions.
verification: A documented JSON schema under docs/, written before the writer
uv run pytest - the exported snippet, executed in a subprocess with only NumPy importable, reproduces the served predictions within the parity harness's prediction tolerance
The same test covers a chain that cannot be folded: the snippet carries the residual preprocessing and still reproduces the predictions
features.evidence: 2026-09-18. Schema first: docs/model-export.md is normative and states the JSON model's fields, the snippet's contract, the residual-chain arithmetic written out, and section 5's tolerance with its measured reason. export.py splits the chain at the last unfoldable step, folds the tail through coefficients_original_units with the estimator's own centring folded into the intercept, carries SNV, MSC (with the reference spectrum it was fitted with) and Normalise as residual steps, and refuses a baseline by name. GET /api/results/{id}/export.json and /export.py serve the two forms; a chain that cannot be carried is a 422 not_exportable with the step's name, not a 500. tests/test_export.py, 9 tests: a foldable chain exports a bare coefficient vector; SNV then Savitzky-Golay then centring carries only the SNV; MSC carries its reference; a range selection folds and leaves the dropped channels at exactly zero weight while the model still takes a full raw spectrum; a classification exports its classes and the 0.5 threshold and the snippet returns labels matching the served assignments; a model below a ten-fold split reproduces both its calibration and its held-out predictions; a baseline and a decomposition are each refused by name. PROPOSAL.md section 9's constraint is held in a subprocess that installs a meta-path finder raising on any import of chemometrics_workbench: the exported file predicts, sys.modules holds nothing of ours, and the predictions agree with the served ones within docs/model-export.md section 5's rtol 1e-4 / atol 1e-6. Measured on the SNV + SG(d1) + centre chain: 6.2e-6 relative, which is the float32 store's contribution that docs/phase-2/exit-run.md measured at 7.09e-6, an order of magnitude inside the stated tolerance. test_server.py covers both endpoints and the 422. `uv run pytest` 889 passed 1 skipped; ruff, format, mypy clean; frontend unchanged, 126 tests and build clean.
features.notes: The tolerance is stated rather than discovered: the application predicts from float32-stored arrays and an export computes in float64, so rtol 1e-4 is an order of magnitude above the largest difference the store can produce rather than a number that happened to pass. If the store ever becomes float64 this should come down to the parity harness's prediction class, and the test holding it is what would notice. A baseline in the residual chain is refused by name - AsLS is a sparse solve per spectrum and does not belong in a copy-pasteable file; the artifact still carries such a model. No UI: the endpoints are the surface, and a download affordance belongs with model-registry's save.

features.title: Two experiments compared step by step
features.user_visible_behavior: Two experiments on one dataset are shown side by side with exactly which pipeline nodes differ - added, removed or edited - and what each scored, so a reader can see that two models differ only in their scatter correction.
verification: pnpm test - the diff of two pipeline snapshots is pure and tested: a node added, a node removed, a parameter changed, and a graph that differs only in layout reported as identical
pnpm exec playwright test - the seeded project compares two experiments and names the node that differs
features.notes: PROPOSAL.md section 8.3 calls this the single feature most likely to make a researcher prefer this tool to a notebook, and says it is free once the model is correct. `Experiment.pipeline_snapshot` is the snapshot by value that makes it possible; `CompareResults` already compares two results and is the screen to build on.

features.title: The exit criterion demonstrated: an exported model predicts in a clean environment
features.user_visible_behavior: Recorded, not built: a fitted model is exported from the served application, its snippet is run in a fresh environment with only NumPy installed, and its predictions agree with the application's within the stated tolerance; and the comparison view is shown naming the one node two models differ by.
verification: A script under tests/ that drives the served application over HTTP, exports the model, runs the snippet in a subprocess with an isolated environment, and compares
Its output committed under docs/phase-3/ with the date, the dataset, the pipeline, every number compared and the tolerance each is judged against
features.notes: The shape Phase 2's exit run set: tests/exit_run.py drives the application over HTTP and writes docs/phase-2/exit-run.md, and this is the same thing for section 16's Phase 3 criterion. The float32 store finding from that run applies here too - an exported snippet computing in float64 will differ from the served numbers at the level docs/phase-2/exit-run.md records, and the tolerance has to be stated with that in mind.
